title: Angle record — the anti-templating control
description: content-engine/angles/{slug}.json. An angle is a materially different customer situation, constraint, or process concern. A place name, landmark, ZIP code, synonym, or reworded heading is NOT an angle. No two pages may hold the same approved angle, and an angle cannot be approved without evidence.

differentiation_verdict.description: NO_SUPPORTED_DIFFERENTIATION is a legitimate and expected outcome. Fewer useful pages beat many thin ones, so it must never be worked around by inventing an angle.

status.description: Lifecycle: proposed -> researched -> evidence_backed -> approved -> used. An angle disproven by research goes to unsupported; one abandoned goes to retired. Only approved and used may be written from.

statement.description: The situation, stated so it would still be meaningful with the city name removed. If masking the place name empties it, it is not an angle.

evidence.description: Pointers to claim ids. Angles cite rather than restate, so a claim's status changes in one place and every angle depending on it re-derives.

blocked_by.description: Open-question ids that must be answered before this angle can move to approved.

source_ids.description: Direct source registry references, in addition to claim-level evidence.

retirement_reason.description: Required when status is unsupported or retired: what the research actually found.

distinctiveness_assessment.description: Whether the situation is genuinely distinct from siblings. A condition created by statewide law is not distinctive — it applies to every page equally.

research_locked.description: True once curated. bootstrap-research.py refuses to overwrite even with --force.
